long_biography.plain_text:
The Kroymans name remained on a Hilversum Ferrari showroom after the group's 2009 collapse, but Frits Kroymans no longer owned it. Friends had preserved the dealership; in 2020 he bought it back. That return followed decades in which he had taken over his father's car business, secured Ferrari representation and built an expansive importer, dealer and leasing operation.

His subsequent holdings are not a revival of the old corporation. Through a family holding, Kroymans has interests in car retail and leasing alongside technical wholesaling, industrial equipment and other businesses. He has remained involved in acquisitions and the holding's development, extending his commercial interests beyond the showroom that first made his name.

uncertainties.detail: The saved owner input links this exact-name Dutch person record to Icarus, and independent yacht pages match the vessel's name, builder and dimensions. Broad exact-name, Dutch-language and builder-combination searches did not yield a public document naming Frits Kroymans as Icarus's legal or beneficial owner. The uncommon name plus Dutch business/geographic match resolves the public entrepreneur at 82 confidence, but the vessel association remains an input-only clue and does not appear in biography, wealth conclusions or tags.

The 2009 receivers' report confirms the old Kroymans Corporation's bankruptcy; independent 2020 reporting says friends maintained the dealership until Frits repurchased it. The later Kroymans Familieholding and Citadel interests are active but not represented as an uninterrupted continuation of the bankrupt corporation.

The family dealership preceded Frits, he succeeded his father, and he later became the old group's sole shareholder and regained the family dealership. This supports medium-confidence family transfer under the succession inference rule. No reliable source documents a will, inherited stake or exact transfer instrument, so Inherited and Inherited and expanded are not asserted despite his well-documented commercial expansion.

Current government and first-party descriptions establish several material sectors, while group-level reported automotive/lease revenue is only one share of the whole. No personal valuation by segment demonstrates one current dominant sector, so Diversified is used. Recent direct interview material describes ongoing attention and acquisitions, supporting Operator, but not a chief-executive title or exclusive daily management.

Published ages in 2020 and 2026 point broadly to the late 1930s or 1940 and are too imprecise to establish a birth year, day or month. Current reporting indicates recent life and activity, but the authoritative mortality value Unknown is preserved rather than silently corrected without a direct vital record.

Mandatory Forbes-first and later exact LinkedIn, Instagram, Personal Website, Facebook, Twitter/X, YouTube, TikTok and Wikipedia searches did not authenticate a personal account or a dedicated Forbes profile. The current company site is proposed only as a Company Website because independent reporting establishes his relationship to that dealership; corporate LinkedIn accounts for the old corporation and namesake relatives are excluded.
